title: microbatch-ordering-induced-beam-sampling-deviation-incident-review
summary: Canary rollout of model v3.2.beta exhibited statistically significant divergence in beam sampling behavior versus baseline. Root cause traced to microbatch reorder + RNG stream mismanagement combined with an alternate fused-sampler kernel path. Immediate rollback to v3.2.alpha restored expected behavior.
impact: Canary cohort (10% of traffic, internal test clusters) produced high-variance outputs: 3x increase in hallucination-rate alarms, reduced beam-consensus, elevated token-level entropy. No customer-facing SLA breaches (rolled back before Dedicated/Hosted expansion). Affected experiments and internal eval pipelines; briefly regressed A/B metric 'factuality_score' in staging.
timeline:
2026-01-16 03:10 UTC — Canary rollout of v3.2.beta started (canary config: 10%, dynamic batching enabled)
2026-01-16 03:18 UTC — Internal A/B eval job flagged token-entropy delta + KL divergence > threshold
2026-01-16 03:20 UTC — Oncall alerted by 'beam_consensus_drop' monitor; manual investigation started
2026-01-16 03:27 UTC — Quick sanity checks: no manifest checksum issues, weight checksums OK
2026-01-16 03:35 UTC — Observed microbatch reorder logs and preemption events correlating with samples showing divergence
2026-01-16 03:45 UTC — Temporary mitigation: disable dynamic microbatching for model v3.2.beta on canary nodes
2026-01-16 03:52 UTC — Canary rollback to v3.2.alpha initiated
2026-01-16 04:05 UTC — Canary rollback completed; metrics returned to baseline over next 15 minutes
2026-01-17 — Begin RCA pairing eng + applied-ml to reproduce in isolated harness
root_cause: Two interacting changes combined to create distributional sampling drift: 1) Scheduler/microbatch optimization introduced request-combining reordering when high-priority requests preempted a microbatch. That reorder logic reused a per-microbatch RNG seed instead of preserving per-example RNG streams. 2) The new fused-sampler kernel compiled for the rollout used a different RNG implementation (xoroshiro vs. the previously used pcg64 variant) and consumed RNG bytes differently when invoked in fused path. Individually these differences were small; together they produced nontrivial shifts in sampling distribution for beam/temperature settings used in our canary tests.
mitigation_steps:
Immediate: rollback to v3.2.alpha for all canary nodes (completed).
Short-term: disable fused-sampler kernel path for this model and pin RNG behavior to legacy stream in the scheduler for canary builds. Re-run canary tests.
Medium-term: enforce explicit per-example RNG state in the microbatch scheduler and add parity tests for RNG paths between kernels. Create unit tests that compare sampling distributions (KL) under both kernel implementations using a fixed set of seeds.
Long-term: add rollout gating that computes sample-level KL divergence between control and candidate for top-K/top-P sampling; abort rollout if divergence exceeds threshold. Update canary check to include beam_consensus and per-token entropy monitors.
long_term_actions:
1) INF-4821: Scheduler: maintain per-request RNG streams and persist RNG state through preemption boundary (owner: eng-serving-runtime).
2) PR 1284: Rework fused-sampler kernel API so RNG consumption is identical to legacy path (owner: applied-ml).
3) Create canary-statistics harness that runs synthetic sampling probes and emits KL/JS divergence metrics to metrics pipeline before opening to traffic (owner: eng-sre).
4) Add e2e test in CI to assert that sampling distributions differ by < 0.5% KL for canonical prompts across kernel variants (owner: developer-experience).
monitoring_changes:
New/updated alerts:
- beam_consensus_drop: alert if average beam overlap < 0.65 over 5min vs baseline
- token_entropy_delta: alert if rolling 1h KL divergence between candidate and control token distribution > 0.02
- per_request_rng_seed_mismatch_rate: log and alert if any microbatch shows >0% seed collisions (should be zero)
Dashboards: add 'Sampling Parity' panel to model rollout dashboard showing KL, JS, entropy, hallucination_rate, and microbatch-preemption frequency.
runbook_updates:
On-call checklist (add to rollout runbook):
1) If beam_consensus_drop fires:
  - Check rollout percent and model variant via console
  - Query logs: 'microbatch.reorder' and 'rng.seed_reused' flags for the model (Loki)
  - If reorder + RNG reuse seen, set rollout to 0% and notify eng-serving-runtime + applied-ml
2) Temporary quick fix: disable dynamic microbatching for the model, or set deterministic sampling (temperature=0) for canary traffic until patch applied
3) If rollback needed: follow standard rollback steps documented at confluence: 'deploy/rollbacks' and tag incident in ticket INF-4821
4) After rollback: run sampling-harness job and attach results to incident ticket.
repro_steps_and_commands:
(Useful queries/playbooks)
- Loki: {app="serving-runtime",model="v3.2.beta"} |= "microbatch.reorder" | json | line_format "%s"
- BigQuery: SELECT microbatch_id, count(*) AS size, any_value(rng_seed_reused) FROM `prod_logs.batch_events` WHERE model="v3.2.beta" AND event_ts BETWEEN TIMESTAMP_SUB(CURRENT_TIMESTAMP(), INTERVAL 1 HOUR) AND CURRENT_TIMESTAMP() GROUP BY microbatch_id;
- Local reproduce (dev harness):
  python tools/sampling_harness.py --model v3.2.beta --prompts testset/sanity_prompts.jsonl --microbatch-schedule preemptive --rng-mode per-microbatch --repeat 1000 --emit-distributions out.json
- Compare distributions:
  python tools/compare_distributions.py out_control.json out_candidate.json --metric kl --threshold 0.02
- Quick toggle to disable fused kernel (example):
  kubectl set env deployment/serving-runtime KERNEL_FUSED_SAMPLER=false -n canary
notes_to_oncall: - This incident was contained in canary because we have low-latency rollout gates — good.\n- Primary lesson: micro-optimizations that change scheduling semantics can have non-obvious impacts on randomized algorithms.\n- Keep communication narrow and technical when escalating to applied-ml; they need deterministic reproducer artifacts (seeds + prompts).
unresolved_questions: - Why did the fused-sampler PR not include an explicit RNG parity test? (owner: applied-ml)\n- Were there any late-night pushes to the scheduler that coincided with the rollout window that changed preemption heuristics? (owner: platform-engineering)\n- Should we mandate RNG compatibility tests as part of kernel integration checklist? (proposal: yes)
commands_and_snippets:
# quick check for seed reuse in logs
kubectl logs -n canary -l app=serving-runtime --since=30m | grep microbatch.reorder | jq '.rng_seed_reused' | sort | uniq -c

# run synthetic KL probe (dev)
python tools/sampling_harness.py --model v3.2.alpha --candidate v3.2.beta --prompts probes/high_variance.jsonl --repeat 2000 --out probe_results.json
python tools/compare_distributions.py probe_results_control.json probe_results_candidate.json --metric kl
